title: Raja Yoga)
hook: you can't see the bottom of a lake while the wind is blowing

segments.voice: Yesterday, Raja Yoga's monkey: restless, drunk on desire, stung by jealousy, possessed by pride. The first lesson was simply to watch it jump.

Stand at the edge of a lake on a windy afternoon. The surface is all chop and glitter. Somewhere down there are stones, weeds, maybe a lost key, but you can't see any of it. Come back at dawn, when the air is still. The same water. Now you can count the pebbles. Nothing was added to the lake overnight. Something was taken away. Vivekananda uses that lake to explain one short line near the start of the Yoga Sutras.
screen: `A LAKE ON A WINDY DAY.` → `THE SAME LAKE AT DAWN.` → `NOTHING ADDED. SOMETHING STILLED.`

segments.voice: Raja Yoga carries, in its second half, Vivekananda's own rendering of the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, short lines with his explanation under each. Near the very start is the line that says what yoga is. Put plainly: yoga is the stilling of the waves of the mind. The Sanskrit word for the mind-stuff is chitta. The word for its waves, the shapes it keeps taking, is vritti. And Vivekananda reaches for a lake. The bottom of the lake, he says, is our own true self. The lake is the chitta, and the waves are the vrittis. While the surface is rippled, we can't see the bottom. If the water is muddy, we can't see it either. Only when the water is clear and the waves die down do we see what was there the whole time. That changes the goal. Nobody has to build a self, or earn one, or go and find one somewhere else. In this picture it's already lying at the bottom, and the work is to let the surface settle. So yesterday's monkey and today's lake belong together. Watching the monkey shows you where the wind is coming from. Stilling the waves is what the watching is for. Vivekananda doesn't pretend it's quick. The waves keep rising: a craving, an insult remembered, a plan for tomorrow. Each one hides the bottom for a while. Each time one settles, the water is a little clearer.
screen: `YOGA STILLS THE WAVES OF THE MIND.` · `THE LAKE IS CHITTA. THE WAVES ARE VRITTIS.` · `THE BOTTOM IS THE TRUE SELF.` · then, large: `LET THE WATER CLEAR.`

segments.voice: Picture a lake, any lake, under a little wind, and each time a thought rises, see it as a wave on that surface. Don't push the wave flat; let it be a wave and watch it pass back into the water, big ones and small ones, and between them, for a moment, the surface may go still. If you pray, you can rest in that stillness as your prayer.
Raja Yoga. Vivekananda's yoga of the mind, which he explains with a lake: still the waves, and the bottom, the true self, was there all along.
Your line: let the water clear. Nothing is added to the lake, only something stilled. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: People who follow Vivekananda's teaching read Patanjali's Yoga Sutras with his explanations and keep a daily sit aimed at quieting the mind; the Ramakrishna Mission and Vedanta Societies hold classes on the text.
